short: The relentless sequence of synchronized Allied offensives that drove the German army back to its borders and forced the Armistice.
full:
Beginning on 8 August 1918 with a crushing British and Commonwealth victory at Amiens, the Allies launched a series of synchronized offensives designed to prevent the German army from regrouping. Utilizing fully integrated all-arms tactics that combined infantry, tanks, aircraft, and precision artillery, the Allied forces systematically dismantled the deeply fortified Hindenburg Line. The coordinated attacks across the breadth of the Western Front left the German command unable to shift reserves to plug the continuous breaches.

Over the next three months, the relentless pressure broke the fighting spirit of the German military and sparked mutinies among their exhausted ranks. As their allies collapsed and revolution broke out at home, the German high command informed their government that the war was lost. The offensive finally concluded on 11 November when the Armistice came into effect, silencing the guns after four years of unprecedented carnage.
